# Nehemiah Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 470v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** This is the account of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, during the twentieth year of the king's reign, I was living in the royal fortress of Susa

**2** when my brother Hanani arrived with some men from Judah. I eagerly questioned them about the Jewish survivors who had returned from exile, and about the state of Jerusalem.

**3** The news they brought was devastating: "The people who survived and returned to the province are in deep trouble and humiliation. Jerusalem's wall lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned to ashes."

**4** When I heard this, I broke down and wept. For days I mourned, going without food and pouring out my heart to the God of heaven.

**5** I prayed, "O LORD, God of heaven — you are the great and awe-inspiring God, the One who faithfully keeps every promise to those who love you and walk in your ways:

**6** Please hear me now! Open your eyes and your ears to the desperate prayer of your servant. Day and night I come before you on behalf of your people Israel. I confess our sins — yes, my own sins and the sins of my family — all that we have committed against you.

**7** We have been utterly unfaithful. We have ignored the commands, the laws, and the decrees you gave through your servant Moses.

**8** But remember what you told Moses: 'If you betray me, I will scatter you across the nations.

**9** Yet if you come back to me and obey my commands, then even if you are exiled to the most distant corners of the earth, I will gather you and bring you home to the place I have chosen for my dwelling.'

**10** These are your people, LORD — your own servants, the ones you rescued with your overwhelming power and mighty hand!

**11** O Lord, please hear my prayer — hear the prayers of all your servants who long to honor your name. Give me success today. Move this man's heart to show me compassion." At that time, I was serving as the king's personal cupbearer.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes
1. **Prayer as theological architecture** — Nehemiah's prayer is a masterful example of covenant theology in action: he appeals to God's character (v. 5), confesses corporate sin (vv. 6-7), invokes God's own promises (vv. 8-9), and claims God's redemptive history (v. 10) before making his request (v. 11).
2. **The power of grief** — Nehemiah's visceral response — weeping, mourning, fasting — reveals that for biblical leaders, passion for God's purposes begins not with strategy but with heartbreak.
3. **"This man"** — The deliberate anonymity of the king underscores a theological point: earthly rulers, however powerful, are instruments in God's hands, subordinate to the divine plan.

*— PNEUMA*
